tables.title: Al₂O₃ development stages contributing to the final training set.
tables.note: 44 sampling blocks; 67,760 tasks; 2,580 final student training geometries.

tables.title: YSZ development stages contributing to the final training set.
tables.note: 47 sampling blocks; 1,740 tasks; 4,272 final student training geometries.

tables.title: MIL-120–CO₂ development stages contributing to the final training set.
tables.note: 57 sampling blocks; 5,538 tasks; 6,041 final student training geometries. The 5,561 high-support selections correspond to 5,547 unique retained geometries. The final teacher subsequently labelled all 6,041 final geometries without further geometry acquisition.

tables.title: Random-route accuracy on unselected configurations
tables.note: Mean ± sample SD over five configuration-selection repeats; force units eV Å⁻¹. Each repeat excludes its full R50. Route codes identify students trained under each supervision scheme: A-T0, A-hybrid, A-TR, A-DFT20 and A-DFTref denote $T_0$, Hybrid, T_R, DFT-20 and DFT-60, respectively.

tables.title: Teacher errors beyond queried geometries
tables.note: Mean ± sample SD over five matched configuration-selection repeats; force units eV Å⁻¹. Each teacher is evaluated on the same forty geometries per repeat, included in expanded student supervision but excluded from teacher adaptation.

tables.title: Force errors on the 120-configuration liquid–amorphous test set.
tables.note: Values are pooled force-component RMSEs in eV Å⁻¹ on the same 120 test geometries and DFT labels. The fixed adapted-teacher router assigns high support at $p$ > 0.1 and low support at $p$ ≤ 0.1; partition errors are shown for the two teachers. The historical expansion students use 940 and 1320 training geometries, respectively, and 100k training steps; they are distinct from the final production students. The adapted teacher remains unchanged during expansion, with no additional target DFT references acquired; teacher adaptation uses 140 target DFT references.

tables.title: Independent-test force errors of the final production students.
tables.note: Force-component RMSEs are in eV Å⁻¹ and pool all Cartesian residuals on the common test set of each system. Both routes use the final 500k-step students. Reduction = 100 × (RMSE_direct − RMSE_DICE)/RMSE_direct, calculated before rounding.

tables.title: Dynamical stability of the final production students.
tables.note: The table reports the earliest recorded instability time for each directly fine-tuned student, determined from the last stored frame. Timesteps are 1 fs for Al₂O₃ and YSZ and 0.5 fs for MIL-120.

tables.title: Endpoint-detrended interior energy-profile errors on nine common DFT paths.
tables.note: MAEs are in meV per P40 framework cell and average the nine interior images of each eleven-image DFT path. Both models are evaluated on the same DFT geometries; $t$ is the normalised cumulative minimum-image Cartesian displacement along that DFT path. The endpoint-linear residual is removed before absolute averaging, as defined above. E-cell denotes the alternate fixed cell.
